Situation
​Patient: Hossam Eldin Mohamed, 45-year-old male
​Location: Discharged from SICU today (Post-operative day 1 of vacuum placement on right hip)
​Current Status: Stable, conscious, well-oriented, normal breathing and nervous system examination. Transitioning with ongoing evaluation for suspected atrial thrombus and pulmonary embolism.
​Background
​Past Medical History:
​Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
​Myasthenia Gravis (on Mestinon 120 mg every 8 hours)
​History of DVT and Pulmonary Embolism (2023)
​Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS)
​Past Surgical History:
​Bilateral hip replacement (2007)
​Recurrent debridement starting from 2022
​Current Admissions Details: Admitted initially to SICU for respiratory distress (hypoxia, wheezy chest) and tachycardia, with a working differential diagnosis of suspected pulmonary embolism.
​Assessment
​CNS & Vitals: Fully conscious, RBS 150 mg/dL, Temp 38°C, Blood Pressure 114/70 mmHg, Heart Rate 67 bpm, Respiratory Rate 21 bpm.
​Respiratory: Bilateral equal air entry (BEAE) with clear chest sounds; SpO2 is 98% on nasal cannula 2 L/min.
​Abdomen & UOP: Abdomen is lax, tolerating oral feeding. Urine output is adequate at 100 mL/hr.
​Extremities & Skin: Infected right hip joint with vacuum placement in situ. Bedridden with a Grade 1 bedsore on the buttocks.
​Recent Investigations & Updates:
​Echocardiogram: Showed a suspected thrombus in the atrium. Cardiology consulted; Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE) is planned for tomorrow.
​Pulmonology: Consulted; advised continuation of inhaled corticosteroids and nebulizers. A CT chest is scheduled for tomorrow.
​Labs: Recent labs completed and scheduled for follow-up review tomorrow.
​Recommendation
​Medications Adjusted: Clexane increased to 80 mg subcutaneously twice daily (already initiated per cardiology advice). Continue baseline medications including Mestinon, antibiotics, antifungals, and steroids as prescribed.
​Diagnostic Plan for Tomorrow:
​Perform Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE).
​Perform CT Chest.
​Follow up on recent lab results.
​Monitoring: Continue close observation of vital signs, oxygenation, and wound/vacuum status post-SICU discharge.

​Mechanism of Injury: High-energy road traffic accident (RTA) resulting in a traumatic left hip fracture-dislocation.

Situation
​Patient: Hossam Eldin Mohamed, 45-year-old male
​Location: Discharged from SICU today (Post-operative day 1 of vacuum placement on right hip)
​Current Status: Stable, conscious, well-oriented, normal breathing and nervous system examination. Transitioning with ongoing evaluation for suspected atrial thrombus and pulmonary embolism.
​Background
​Past Medical History:
​Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
​Myasthenia Gravis (on Mestinon 120 mg every 8 hours)
​History of DVT and Pulmonary Embolism (2023)
​Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS)
​Past Surgical History:
​Bilateral hip replacement (2007)
​Recurrent debridement starting from 2022
​Current Admissions Details: Admitted initially to SICU for respiratory distress (hypoxia, wheezy chest) and tachycardia, with a working differential diagnosis of suspected pulmonary embolism.
​Assessment
​CNS & Vitals: Fully conscious, RBS 150 mg/dL, Temp 38°C, Blood Pressure 114/70 mmHg, Heart Rate 67 bpm, Respiratory Rate 21 bpm.
​Respiratory: Bilateral equal air entry (BEAE) with clear chest sounds; SpO2 is 98% on nasal cannula 2 L/min.
​Abdomen & UOP: Abdomen is lax, tolerating oral feeding. Urine output is adequate at 100 mL/hr.
​Extremities & Skin: Infected right hip joint with vacuum placement in situ. Bedridden with a Grade 1 bedsore on the buttocks.
​Recent Investigations & Updates:
​Echocardiogram: Showed a suspected thrombus in the atrium. Cardiology consulted; Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE) is planned for tomorrow.
​Pulmonology: Consulted; advised continuation of inhaled corticosteroids and nebulizers. A CT chest is scheduled for tomorrow.
​Labs: Recent labs completed and scheduled for follow-up review tomorrow.
​Recommendation
​Medications Adjusted: Clexane increased to 80 mg subcutaneously twice daily (already initiated per cardiology advice). Continue baseline medications including Mestinon, antibiotics, antifungals, and steroids as prescribed.
​Diagnostic Plan for Tomorrow:
​Perform Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE).
​Perform CT Chest.
​Follow up on recent lab results.
​Monitoring: Continue close observation of vital signs, oxygenation, and wound/vacuum status post-SICU discharge.
